scorecard.title: Product pages with fewer than 2 images
scorecard.recommendation: Add a second image (pack shot or brew detail) — single-image PDPs read as unfinished and convert worse.

scorecard.title: Product pages with a short description
scorecard.recommendation: Add tasting notes, origin and brew guidance — under 200 characters gives a shopper nothing to justify the price.
scorecard.evidence: products.json `body_html` stripped to text, length in characters

scorecard.title: Colour variants missing their own image
scorecard.recommendation: No action — this catalogue has no colour-option products to check.
scorecard.evidence: no product option named Colour/Color found in products.json

scorecard.title: Core pack sizes sold out
scorecard.recommendation: Prioritise restocking the middle pack sizes first — the smallest (trial) and largest (bulk) sizes selling through last is normal; the middle going out isn't.
scorecard.evidence: products.json Size option values, ordered; middle 50% flagged sold out

scorecard.title: Sold-out PDPs with no back-in-stock capture
scorecard.recommendation: Turn on a back-in-stock signup on these PDPs — this store already runs a generic capture mechanism on other pages (no `swym` marker found), so intent is being lost only where it's switched off.
scorecard.evidence: PDP HTML sampled for 20 highest-leakage sold-out products; searched for swym/back in stock/notify me/restock/klaviyo-bis/bis markers

scorecard.title: Shipping / refund policy verification
scorecard.recommendation: This store's robots.txt disallows `/policies/*` for all bots, so a compliant scanner — and any AI shopping agent or price-comparison tool that honours robots.txt — can't verify your shipping/refund terms programmatically. Consider allowing those two specific paths if you want that trust signal visible to automated buyers.
scorecard.evidence: robots.txt Disallow: /policies/ and /*/policies/ for User-agent: *; both paths return 200 when fetched directly, but were not fetched by this scan

limits: scores are indices, not currency: public storefront data carries no order-volume or revenue signal
trust/policies check skipped for shipping and refund pages: robots.txt disallows /policies/* for bots on this store
collection membership recorded for 20/225 collections in this fixture set; rest treated as empty (fixture-recording bound, not a live-scan limitation)
A1: public storefront JSON reflects live availability; can lag minutes behind actual stock
A2: collection order approximates merchandising intent; bestseller-style handles approximate demand
A3: a sold-out variant on a merchandised product is intent lost; we cannot see how much
A4: detection of back-in-stock capture by HTML markers is approximate (themes vary)
A5: assumes the reviewer runs on macOS/Linux with Node >=20
